sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: When producer Ellie Gordon Marshall was growing up, she played baseball, tennis, soccer,
sentences.zh: 当制作人埃莉·戈登·马歇尔长大时，她打过棒球、网球、足球、

sentences.en: ice hockey, field hockey, flag football, volleyball, field lacrosse, box lacrosse.
sentences.zh: 冰球、草地曲棍球、旗帜橄榄球、排球、室外长曲棍球、室内长曲棍球。

sentences.en: I don't even know what that one is.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道最后那个是什么。

sentences.en: Basically, I played whatever I could find.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我能找到什么就玩什么。

sentences.en: If there's a team, a moving object, and points to be had, I'm probably pretty good at it.
sentences.zh: 只要有队伍、有移动的物体、还有得分的机会，我可能都很擅长。

sentences.en: Ellie is an only child, and she didn't really think of her parents as sports people.
sentences.zh: 埃莉是个独生女，她并不觉得父母是那种热爱运动的人。

sentences.en: To be fair, my dad sometimes went out for runs, but in short shorts I found very embarrassing,
sentences.zh: 平心而论，我爸爸有时会去跑步，但他穿的短裤让我觉得非常尴尬，
所以我把这记忆屏蔽了。

sentences.en: You have to take care of yourself in this world.
sentences.zh: 在这个世界上，你必须照顾好自己。

sentences.en: Still, for years, I thought I was the only one in my family that truly understood the appeal
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，多年来我一直以为我是家里唯一一个真正理解运动中的

sentences.en: of the sweat, blood, and tears of sport.
sentences.zh: 汗水、鲜血和泪水的魅力的人。

sentences.en: That is until I came across my mom's high school yearbooks.
sentences.zh: 直到我偶然翻到我妈妈的高中毕业纪念册。

sentences.en: So you guys were called the Rockettes.
sentences.zh: 所以你们当时叫“火箭队”。

sentences.en: And the boys were called the Rockettes.
I wouldn't say the Rocks, but yeah.
sentences.zh: 我不会说叫“岩石队”，但确实是。

sentences.en: This is me talking to my mom a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 这是几年前我和我妈妈交谈时的录音。

sentences.en: We were poring over memories from her time on the high school basketball team, back in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我们正在仔细翻阅她 20 世纪 60 年代在高中女子篮球队时的回忆。

sentences.en: The team ended the season with a 9-16 record.
sentences.zh: 球队以 9 胜 16 负的战绩结束了赛季。

sentences.en: In one photo, all the girls are sitting straight-legged on the gym floor.
sentences.zh: 在其中一张照片中，所有女孩都双腿笔直地坐在体育馆的地板上。

sentences.en: They're in sort of a semicircle around a basketball, showing off their striped socks.
sentences.zh: 她们围着一个篮球呈半圆形坐着，展示着她们的条纹袜子。

sentences.en: There's also photos of the team goofing around, which I love, but my favorite picture of my mom
sentences.zh: 还有一些队员们在恶作剧的照片，我非常喜欢，但我最喜欢我妈妈的那张照片

sentences.en: is her at practice leaping up to defend a player she still remembers.
sentences.zh: 是她在训练中跃起防守一位她至今仍记得的球员。

sentences.en: This is Donna Krause, who was like the star on the team.
sentences.zh: 这是唐娜·克劳斯，她就像是队里的明星。

sentences.en: She's shooting a basket, and you can tell there's no way I'm going to block her shot.
sentences.zh: 她正在投篮，你能看出我根本不可能盖掉她的球。

sentences.en: In the practice photos, everyone looks so cool and athletic with their white sneakers and socks.
sentences.zh: 在训练照片中，每个人穿着白色的运动鞋和袜子，看起来都那么酷、那么有运动气息。

sentences.en: But in the game photos, some things looked off.
sentences.zh: 但在比赛照片中，有些地方看起来怪怪的。

sentences.en: The tops, they were kind of cropped tops so that when you, you know, shot a basket or moved your arms up,
sentences.zh: 上衣，它们有点像露脐装，所以当你，你知道的，投篮或者把手臂往上抬时，

sentences.en: you could actually see your stomach.
sentences.zh: 你真的能看到自己的肚子。

sentences.en: Yeah, her entire midriff is exposed.
sentences.zh: 对，她的整个腹部都露出来了。

sentences.en: And I remember looking at these when I was a teenager and such a tomboy.
sentences.zh: 我记得当我还是个十几岁、性格像假小子的小女孩时看到这些照片。

sentences.en: Yeah, horrified because when I saw the uniforms, I could not imagine playing any sport at that age
sentences.zh: 是的，吓坏了，因为当我看到那些队服时，我无法想象自己在这个年纪，

sentences.en: in a satiny shirt that barely covered my stomach.
sentences.zh: 穿着一件几乎遮不住肚子的缎面衬衫去进行任何体育运动。

sentences.en: And that wasn't the only thing my mom told me that sounded weird about her days playing basketball.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我妈妈告诉我的关于她打篮球的岁月里听起来很奇怪的唯一事情。

sentences.en: Ellie's mom played basketball, but not the five-on-five basketball we know today.
sentences.zh: 埃莉的妈妈打过篮球，但不是我们今天所知的五人制篮球。

sentences.en: She played six-on-six Iowa girls basketball.
sentences.zh: 她打的是爱荷华州六人制女子篮球。

sentences.en: There were three forwards and three guards.
sentences.zh: 场上有三个前锋和三个后卫。

sentences.en: So as the three guards, you guarded the other team's three forwards.
sentences.zh: 作为三个后卫之一，你要防守对方球队的三个前锋。

sentences.en: In six-on-six basketball, the three forwards only play offense.
sentences.zh: 在六人制篮球中，三个前锋只打进攻。

sentences.en: And the three guards only play defense.
No one is allowed to leave their assigned half of the court.
sentences.zh: 任何人都不允许离开自己被分配的半场。

sentences.en: I was a guard, so I never shot any baskets.
sentences.zh: 我是个后卫，所以我从来不投篮。

sentences.en: All I did was try to prevent people from shooting baskets.
sentences.zh: 我唯一做的就是阻止别人投篮。

sentences.en: Six-on-six still uses the full length of a basketball court, but in a different way than five-on-five.
sentences.zh: 六人制仍然使用篮球场的全长，但方式与五人制不同。

sentences.en: In six-player, three forwards from one team and three guards from the opposing team play at one end of the court.
sentences.zh: 在六人制中，一支球队的三名前锋和对方球队的三名后卫在球场的一端打球。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, their teammates wait at the half-court line.
sentences.zh: 同时，他们的队友在中线等待。

sentences.en: So as a guard, I mean, my big role was to get the ball and get it down to the other half court so it would be in the hands of our forwards.
sentences.zh: 所以作为后卫，我的主要任务就是抢到球并把它传到另一半场，这样球就会落入我们前锋的手中。

sentences.en: If a team play in offense makes a basket, the ref throws the ball back to the opposing team's forwards, and now they have a chance to score at the other end of the court.
sentences.zh: 如果进攻方投进一球，裁判会把球扔回给对方球队的前锋，现在他们有机会在球场的另一端得分了。

sentences.en: Another way to think about it, it's like two games of three-on-three with the same ball being tossed back and forth.
sentences.zh: 换个角度想，这就像是两场三对三的比赛，用的是同一个被来回抛接的球。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that was kind of peculiar is you could only dribble the ball twice, and then you had to do something with it.
sentences.zh: 还有一件比较奇怪的事是，你只能运球两次，然后你就必须把球传出去或做别的处理。

sentences.en: At the same time Ellie's mom was playing six-on-six, the boys in her high school were playing five-on-five.
sentences.zh: 在埃莉的妈妈打六人制篮球的同时，她高中的男生们在打五人制篮球。

sentences.en: Just what was your perception of the rules when you started playing, or did you have any?
sentences.zh: 你刚开始打球时对规则有什么看法，或者说你有什么看法吗？

sentences.en: My perception was there were rules for the girls, and there were rules for the boys, and they were different.
sentences.zh: 我的看法是，女孩有女孩的规则，男孩有男孩的规则，而且它们是不同的。

sentences.en: And I don't have a memory of feeling like, oh, I wish we could play the boys' rules.
sentences.zh: 我不记得当时有过诸如“噢，真希望我们能打男孩的规则”这种想法。

sentences.en: It was just kind of like, those were our rules.
sentences.zh: 就好像，那些就是我们的规则。

sentences.en: I was 13 when I first found my mom's yearbook.
sentences.zh: 我 13 岁时第一次发现我妈妈的毕业纪念册。

sentences.en: And to my teenage ears, this sport sounded confusing and so boring.
sentences.zh: 在我的青少年耳朵听来，这项运动听起来令人困惑而且非常无聊。

sentences.en: When the ball is not in your end of the court, do you what, just stand there?
sentences.zh: 当球不在你们那半场时，你该怎么办，就站在那儿吗？

sentences.en: What's fun about being a guard if you can never shoot?
sentences.zh: 如果你永远不能投篮，当后卫有什么意思？

sentences.en: Not to mention the rules reeked of sexism.
sentences.zh: 更不用说这些规则充满了性别歧视。

sentences.en: As if Iowans felt they needed to invent a less rigorous version of basketball made just for the girls.
sentences.zh: 就好像爱荷华州人觉得他们需要发明一种专为女孩量身打造的、不那么严苛的篮球版本。

sentences.en: But even so, Ellie's mom insisted that girls' six-on-six basketball was extremely popular.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，埃莉的妈妈坚称女孩的六人制篮球非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: Not just at her high school, but all over Iowa.
sentences.zh: 不仅在她自己的高中，在整个爱荷华州都是如此。

sentences.en: My memory is the stands being filled, like my mother.
sentences.zh: 我的记忆里看台总是坐得满满的，就像我母亲一样。

sentences.en: And I think most times she brought her knitting because she would get nervous and then she would be knitting away.
sentences.zh: 而且我想大多数时候她都带着她的织物，因为她会感到紧张，然后她就会一直织个不停。

sentences.en: At the girls' games, the gyms in Iowa would be packed.
sentences.zh: 在女子比赛期间，爱荷华州的体育馆总是挤得水泄不通。

sentences.en: And not just with knitting mothers.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是织毛衣的妈妈们。

sentences.en: Entire towns would come out to cheer for their team.
sentences.zh: 整个小镇都会出动为他们的球队呐喊助威。

sentences.en: In fact, it wasn't until my mom left Iowa that she realized this kind of enthusiasm for a girls' sport was rare.
sentences.zh: 事实上，直到我妈妈离开艾奥瓦州，她才意识到这种对女子体育的热情是多么罕见。

sentences.en: That it was regarded as important as boys' basketball I didn't think was unusual.
sentences.zh: 它被认为和男子篮球一样重要，我并不觉得这有什么不寻常。

sentences.en: I thought that that was just the way the world worked.
sentences.zh: 我以为世界本来就是这样的。

sentences.en: My whole life, women and girls' sports have been on the defensive.
sentences.zh: 在我的一生中，妇女和女孩的体育运动一直处于守势。

sentences.en: Always put in a position to prove its worth.
sentences.zh: 总是被迫去证明自己的价值。

sentences.en: So I truly could not comprehend what my mom was describing.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的无法理解我妈妈所描述的那种情景。

sentences.en: A girls' sport with weird sexist rules having just as much, if not more, success than the boys.
sentences.zh: 一项有着奇怪性别歧视规则的女子运动，其成功程度甚至不亚于男子运动，甚至犹有过之。

sentences.en: So for years, I wrote the sport off.
sentences.zh: 所以多年来，我对这项运动不屑一顾。

sentences.en: Because the more I looked into it, the more I realized that my mom wasn't just some six-on-six fanatic.
sentences.zh: 因为我越深入了解，就越意识到我妈妈不仅仅是一个六人制篮球的狂热爱好者。

sentences.en: The game and its rules were popular in Iowa for nearly a century.
sentences.zh: 这项比赛及其规则在艾奥瓦州流行了近一个世纪。

sentences.en: But the sport would ultimately be upended by a federal law designed to end gender discrimination.
sentences.zh: 但这项运动最终将被一项旨在消除性别歧视的联邦法律所颠覆。

sentences.en: The story of the rise and fall of Iowa girls' six-on-six starts with the establishment of women's basketball in 1892.
sentences.zh: 艾奥瓦州女子六人制篮球兴衰的故事始于1892年女子篮球的创立。

sentences.en: Women's basketball is the most fascinating sport because women started playing it almost at exactly the same time men started playing it.
sentences.zh: 女子篮球是最迷人的运动，因为女性开始玩这项运动的时间几乎与男性完全同步。

sentences.en: And they started playing it at a time when the rules were shifting very quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且她们开始接触这门运动时，规则正在发生极快的变化。

sentences.en: This is basketball historian Pamela Grundy.
sentences.zh: 这位是篮球历史学家帕梅拉·格兰迪。

sentences.en: She says even back when James Naismith invented basketball, the rules were still in flux.
sentences.zh: 她说，甚至早在詹姆斯·奈史密斯发明篮球时，规则也还在不断变化中。
一开始是没有运球这一说的。

sentences.en: Free throws didn't exist at firSt.

sentences.zh: 那些也是后来才发明的。

sentences.en: And what happened with women, the fact that the game was very unshaped at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 而对于女性而言，这项运动在最初极具塑造性，

sentences.en: meant that they could shape it in a way that was acceptable for women to play.
sentences.zh: 意味着她们可以将其塑造成适合女性参与的形态。

sentences.en: A phys ed teacher from Smith College named Senda Berenson is credited with being the mother of women's basketball.
sentences.zh: 史密斯学院的一位体育教师森达·贝伦森被公认为女子篮球之母。

sentences.en: She learned of Naismith's new game, invented just miles down the road,
sentences.zh: 她得知了奈史密斯这项几英里外刚刚发明的新运动，

sentences.en: and thought it would be a good fit for her all-women's gym class,
sentences.zh: 认为这很适合她所在的纯女性体操课，

sentences.en: even though team sports for women were practically unheard of in the late 1800s.
sentences.zh: 尽管在19世纪后期，女性参加团队运动几乎闻所未闻。

sentences.en: Basketball was something that allowed women to play on a team, to run around,
sentences.zh: 篮球让女性得以组队玩耍、四处奔跑，

sentences.en: to really be vigorous in a way that traditional women's physical activity didn't allow one to do.
sentences.zh: 以一种传统女性体育活动所不允许的方式尽情挥洒活力。

sentences.en: So it was something, it was a revelation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场革命，是一个全新的启示。

sentences.en: And you look at the pictures and you listen,
sentences.zh: 你看看那些照片，听听看，

sentences.en: talk to what women said about playing basketball back in those early days.
sentences.zh: 了解一下当年那些女性对打篮球的评价。

sentences.en: And it was just the most amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 那简直是最美妙的事情了。

sentences.en: Women's colleges promoted exercise for their students,
sentences.zh: 女子学院鼓励学生们进行锻炼，

sentences.en: but they also stressed that physical education should not interfere with Christian ideals of womanhood,
sentences.zh: 但他们也强调，体育教育不应干涉基督教对女性气质的理想，

sentences.en: such as purity, obedience, and domesticity.
Even Berenson, a true evangelist for women's physical movement,
sentences.zh: 即使是女性身体运动的真正倡导者别伦森，

sentences.en: was deeply concerned that women's basketball never veer outside friendly play.
sentences.zh: 也深感担忧，生怕女子篮球赛偏离了友谊第一的轨道。

sentences.en: She wanted her rules to favor civility over competition.
sentences.zh: 她希望自己的规则能让文明礼貌胜过激烈竞争。

sentences.en: Initially, Senda Berenson made rules that made the women's game a little bit different,
sentences.zh: 最初，森达·别伦森制定的规则让女子比赛显得有些不同，

sentences.en: made rules that made the game seem a little more sedate,
sentences.zh: 她制定的规则让比赛看起来更加温和，

sentences.en: have a little less physical contact.
In this early iteration of women's basketball,
sentences.zh: 在女子篮球的早期演变中，

sentences.en: the court was divided into three zones,
sentences.zh: 球场被划分为三个区域，

sentences.en: nine players on each team passing the ball from zone to zone,
sentences.zh: 每支队伍有九名队员在各个区域间传球，

sentences.en: There was no grabbing at the ball, no more than three dribbles,
sentences.zh: 比赛中不能抢球，运球不得超过三次，

sentences.en: and the winning team had to host a dinner for the defeated team.
sentences.zh: 而且获胜的队伍必须为失败的队伍举办一场晚宴。

sentences.en: Berenson continued to refine the rules at the turn of the century,
sentences.zh: 世纪之交时，别伦森继续完善这些规则，

sentences.en: but by then women's basketball had already spread throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 但到那时，女子篮球已经传遍了全国。

sentences.en: And one of the places it found a foothold was rural Iowa.
sentences.zh: 它站稳脚跟的地方之一就是艾奥瓦州的乡村。

sentences.en: Basketball was a good fit for rural Iowa.
sentences.zh: 篮球非常适合艾奥瓦州的乡村。

sentences.en: It needed limited equipment and could be played indoors in the winter.
sentences.zh: 它对器材要求不高，冬季还可以在室内进行。

sentences.en: It was an easy activity for these tiny towns to rally around.
sentences.zh: 对于这些小镇来说，这是一项很容易凝聚人心的活动。

sentences.en: Little towns of 200, 300 people, they played basketball.
sentences.zh: 只有两三百人的小镇也在打篮球。

sentences.en: See, cities in Iowa did not play any kind of sports until after mid-century.
sentences.zh: 你看，艾奥瓦州的城市直到世纪中叶之后才开始开展任何体育运动。

sentences.en: This is Max McElwain, an academic, former sports reporter, and native Iowan.
sentences.zh: 这位是马克·麦克埃尔温，一名学者、前体育记者，也是艾奥瓦州本地人。

sentences.en: Max told me that while people in the city were debating whether sports were appropriate for girls,
sentences.zh: 马克告诉我，当城里人在争论体育运动是否适合女孩时，

sentences.en: that just wasn't a concern in small-town Iowa.
sentences.zh: 这在艾奥瓦州的小镇根本不成问题。
她们很可能都是农场女孩。

sentences.en: They were likely having to do all sorts of physical chores on their farMs.
sentences.zh: 她们很可能必须在农场里做各种体力农活。

sentences.en: And there wasn't that sort of bifurcation between being an athlete and being feminine.
sentences.zh: 因此，运动员身份和女性气质之间并不存在那种割裂。

sentences.en: In the first few decades of Iowa girls basketball, the rules could differ from county to county.
sentences.zh: 在艾奥瓦州女子篮球发展的头几十年里，比赛规则因县而异。

sentences.en: Some were six-player, some eight or nine.
sentences.zh: 有些是六人制，有些是八人或九人制。

sentences.en: All the iterations were inspired by Senda Berenson's sedate rules, but with one big exception.
sentences.zh: 所有这些变体都受森达·别伦森温和规则的启发，但有一个重大例外。

sentences.en: Iowans wanted their teams to win.
sentences.zh: 艾奥瓦人希望他们的球队获胜。

sentences.en: They wanted the girls to compete, just like the boys.
sentences.zh: 他们希望女孩们像男孩一样去竞争。

sentences.en: In 1920, the Des Moines Register, the largest newspaper in the state, sponsored the first Iowa girls high school basketball tournament.
sentences.zh: 1920年，该州最大的报纸《得梅因纪事报》赞助了第一届艾奥瓦州女子高中篮球锦标赛。

sentences.en: And despite the event being hosted in the big city, only teams from tiny rural towns were invited.
sentences.zh: 尽管这项赛事在大城市举办，但只有来自偏远乡村小镇的球队受邀参加。

sentences.en: Other states also launched similar tournaments around this time.
sentences.zh: 其他州也在这一时期推出了类似赛事。

sentences.en: College-educated PE teachers in the mold of Senda Berenson saw this increase in girls competition, and they were alarmed.
sentences.zh: 受森达·别伦森影响、接受过大学教育的体育老师们看到女子比赛的这种增长，感到十分惊恐。

sentences.en: To them, girls basketball was supposed to be fun and active, but never motivated by winning, and certainly not played in front of audiences.
sentences.zh: 对她们来说，女子篮球本该充满乐趣与活力，但不应以取胜为动力，更不能在观众面前比赛。

sentences.en: They looked around at the competition in men's sports and saw these intense rivalries and violence, and wanted something different for women.
sentences.zh: 她们看着男子体育赛事的竞争，看到了激烈的对抗和暴力，希望为女性寻找一种不同的运动。

sentences.en: So, as a result, at the same time basketball was gaining popularity around the country, there was a major backlash.
sentences.zh: 因此，在篮球全国普及的同时，也出现了强烈的反对浪潮。

sentences.en: A counter-movement of people like Berenson that lobbied school administrators and athletic organizers to keep competition out of girls' sports.
sentences.zh: 这是一场以贝伦森等人为首的反运动，他们游说学校管理者和体育组织者，将竞争排除在女子体育之外。

sentences.en: There start to be conflict between these physical educators and these sort of local communities who've started these tournaments.
sentences.zh: 这些体育教育工作者与发起这些锦标赛的当地社区之间开始出现冲突。

sentences.en: And physical educators really push to eliminate girls' tournaments and to tamp down competition for girls.
sentences.zh: 体育教育工作者极力主张取消女子锦标赛，并压制女性参与竞争。

sentences.en: And so you'll have these statewide battles over this.
sentences.zh: 因此，各州为此展开了激烈的辩论和对抗。

sentences.en: And in many cases, the people pushing to end competition for girls, they win.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，那些力主终止女子竞争的人获胜了。

sentences.en: So there are states where the girls' state tournaments and girls' competition in general just gets eliminated.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些州的女子州锦标赛以及普遍的女子比赛直接被取消了。

sentences.en: Physical educators influence the legislatures to say, no, we will not have this.
sentences.zh: 体育教育工作者施加影响，让立法机关表态拒绝开展这项运动。

sentences.en: We're not going to have a girls' tournament.
And so, in 1925, there was this big meeting in Iowa with the high school administrators about ending girls' basketball.
sentences.zh: 于是，在1925年，爱荷华州的高中管理者们召开了一场关于终结女子篮球的大型会议。

sentences.en: Cities like Des Moines were easily persuaded to shut down their prograMs.

sentences.en: Iowa's small towns were fiercely protective of girls' basketball.

sentences.en: They resented this kind of outside interference.

sentences.en: So, in that big meeting that decided the fate of the sport, a group of educators and coaches dissented.
sentences.zh: 因此，在那场决定该运动命运的大会上，一群教育工作者和教练发出了异议。

sentences.en: It's hard to do much research on this without coming across a famous quote from the meeting.

sentences.en: Gentlemen, if you attempt to do away with girls' basketball in Iowa,

sentences.en: So, you have this group of rebels who really support girls' basketball.

sentences.en: We will leave and we're going to start our own association and we're going to have our own tournament.

sentences.en: And that's the beginning of the real, you know, flowering of Iowa high school girls' basketball.
sentences.zh: 这也是爱荷华州高中女子篮球真正迎来繁荣的起点。

sentences.en: The rebels who supported girls' basketball started the first girls' athletic union in the country.
sentences.zh: 支持女子篮球的叛逆者们创立了全国第一个女子运动联合会。
